title: Copy the image when using Copy in a webview context menu
body: Fixes #292567 ### Problem Right clicking an image in a webview and choosing **Copy** puts nothing on the clipboard. Selecting the image first and then copying works, which is the clue to what is going on. The webview context menu's `Copy` is the standard `CopyAction`, routed to `webview.copy()` in `webview.contribution.ts`, which sends an `execCommand` message that the webview shell runs as `contentDocument.execCommand('copy')`. That only ever copies the *text selection*. Right clicking an image does not create a selection, so there is nothing to copy — and no error, which is why the issue reports silence rather than a failure. ### Fix Track the element the context menu was opened on in `pre/index.html`. When `copy` arrives with a collapsed selection and that element is an ``, encode it as a png and write it with `navigator.clipboard.write` instead of running `execCommand`. Details worth noting: - **Selection still wins.** If the user actually has something selected we fall straight through to `execCommand`, so selecting an image and copying behaves exactly as before. Cut, paste, undo and redo are untouched. - **Cross origin images.** Most webview images are served by the webview service worker, which synthesises the response, so drawing them into a canvas works directly. An image fetched from a genuinely opaque cross origin response taints the canvas and `toBlob` throws, so we fall back to re-requesting it in cors mode and going through `createImageBitmap`. - **Focus.** `navigator.clipboard.write` rejects unless the document is focused, and copy is dispatched as the context menu is closing. We give focus a moment to come back, but still attempt the write if it does not, so we never silently do nothing. - **Staleness.** The tracked image is cleared on the next click or keypress, so a later keyboard copy with nothing selected does not resurrect an image the user right clicked earlier. ### Testing The two encode paths were measured in a webview on VS Code 1.108 with a probe extension: drawing a `vscode-resource` image into a canvas succeeds (`ok: true`), and the cors re-fetch fallback also succeeds (`fetchStatus: 200`, `ok: true`). The end to end context menu flow has not been exercised against a build of this branch — I would appreciate a check on Windows and Linux in particular, where the context menu is rendered differently and the focus timing may not match macOS. ### Related The same missing cors fallback exists in three other copy-image implementations that each grew independently — `markdown-language-features`, `media-preview`, and the notebook webview. A remote image in a markdown preview fails there today with `SecurityError: Tainted canvases may not be exported`. Not touched here; happy to follow up if it is worth consolidating.

## Description

Session pills (changes, PRs, issues, artifacts, references, customizations, browsers, subagents) describe the whole session, but were also rendered under a subagent chat's transcript — where they read as the subagent's own work.

The row is now hidden while a subagent chat is viewed, gated at the shared `ChatInputPills` `enabled` observable in the two hosts that own it:

- **`sessionChatInputToolbar.ts`** (Agents Window) — new `_isSubagentChat` derived following the layer's existing convention (`chat.origin?.kind === ChatOriginKind.Tool`). The pills debug overlay still forces the row visible.
- **`agentHostSessionInputPills.ts`** (chat editor + view pane) — resolves the viewed chat channel and checks `isSubagentChatUri`. Covers both addressing forms the subagent editor uses: the `subagentChatResource` query param, and the canonical fragment-only form resolved through session state. The resolution previously inlined in `getAgentHostSessionBrowserOwnerIds` is extracted into `getAgentHostSessionChatResource` and shared, so the two paths cannot drift.

```ts
// sessionChatInputToolbar.ts
const pillsEnabled = derived(reader => this._debugData.read(reader) !== undefined
    || (turnStatusPillsEnabled.read(reader) && !this._isSubagentChat.read(reader)));
```

Hiding produces the same state as a chat with no pill data, so layout is unchanged: the Agents Window keeps its static height reservation, and the workbench host releases `persistentContentHeight` as it already does when empty.

Per-turn pills (`ChatTurnPillsWidget`) are untouched — they describe a single turn's own changes, which is legitimate inside a subagent transcript. Fork, side, and peer chats keep their pills.

Tests cover both surfaces: a single widget navigating session → subagent (both URI forms) → back, asserting pills and reserved height; and the Agents Window toolbar across main, subagent, and fork chats.

title: Agents - Add New Session to the Side
body:
Fixes #334508

### What

Adds **New Session to the Side**: opens a new session beside the active one instead of replacing it.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/740e962a-bfa0-4914-a8c7-b29746441674

### How to use it

| Gesture | Result |
|---|---|
| Click **New** | New session in place (unchanged) |
| **`⌥⌘N`** / `Ctrl+Alt+N` | New session to the side |
| **Alt+click** on **New** | New session to the side |
| Click the **▾** chevron | Menu: *New Session to the Side*, *New Quick Chat*, *New Chat in This Session* |

### Why `⌥⌘N`

`Alt` is already the "to the side" modifier in this window (`Alt+click` on a session row, `Alt`-invoke in the Side Chats menu), so `⌥` + `⌘N` reads as "New Session, to the side". The only overlap is *New Untitled File* on web/non-Windows, which stays reachable — ours is weighted `SessionsContrib` and scoped to `!editorAreaFocus`, the same layering the existing `⌘N` already uses.

### Implementation

- `ISessionsService.openNewSession({ toSide })` anchors the new slot to the right of the active session via `insertAt`.
- The **New** button becomes a `ButtonWithDropdown`; the chevron opens the new `Menus.NewSessionDropdown`.

The grid caps at one empty composer slot, so if one already exists elsewhere it is activated where it sits rather than duplicated. That is covered by a test.

### Second commit: unrelated layout bug this surfaced

Submitting a draft while two sessions were visible popped the Changes/Files panel open. `SinglePaneExistingSessionStrategy` revealed the detail panel for any created session in its multi-session branch, missing the submit exclusion that the single-session branch already has. Reachable before this PR (pin a session, then `⌘N`), but this feature makes it the common path, so it is fixed here in a separate commit.

### Testing

`351 passing, 0 failing` across the sessions, layout and actions suites. The layout regression test was verified to fail without its fix.

title: Agents: no way to open a new session beside the current one

labels.name: feature-request

labels.name: insiders-released

body:
### Problem

In the Agents window, **New** (`⌘N`) always replaces the session in the active slot. When you're already working in a session and want to open a second one and work in both, there's no single gesture for it — you have to rearrange the grid yourself, in one of two ways:

- Take an **existing** session, move it to the side, and *then* click **New**; or
- Click **New** — which replaces what you were looking at — and *then* find the session you were working in and move **that** one to the side.

Either way it's a two-step detour, and the second one makes you lose sight of your session before you get it back.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Open a session in the Agents window.
2. Press `⌘N` (or click **New**).

**Current:** the composer replaces the session you were looking at.
**Expected:** a way to keep the current session visible and start the new one next to it, in one action.

### Why it matters

The grid already supports side-by-side sessions — `Alt+click` on a row in the sessions list opens an *existing* session to the side — but there's no equivalent for creating a *new* one. Comparing two agents on the same task, or kicking off a second session while the first is still running, is a common flow that currently costs an extra manual rearrange.

### Proposal

- A **New Session to the Side** command with a keybinding.
- Reachable from the **New** button without adding a second button — e.g. a split button, plus `Alt+click` to match the `Alt` = "to the side" convention the window already uses.

title: Agent Host: Smoke test Dev Container sessions
body:
## Summary

Add an end-to-end Agents Window smoke test that starts a session on an Agent Host inside a Dev Container.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Run wherever Linux Docker is available**: The suite probes `docker info` for a reachable daemon with `OSType=linux`. Linux CI asserts this capability and fails if it is missing; macOS and Windows run the suite when capable and otherwise skip it. This keeps local Docker Desktop/Colima coverage without hard-coding CI platforms.
- **Prove the execution location and full turn path**: The test waits for the mock `OK` response, requires an AHP connection logged with `vscode.clientConnectionKind=dev_container` / `transport=devcontainer`, and requires an invocation targeting a `remote-devcontainer__…` session resource.
- **Handle mutually exclusive creation controls**: The automation clears New Worktree when selected before waiting for Dev Container availability, using checkbox ARIA state rather than transient CSS classes.
- **Support unpublished packaged commits**: Product CI builds have a commit hash that is not available from update.code.visualstudio.com. The fixture preinstalls the latest published CLI and the fallback finder emits the validated tilde-form path expected by the installer.
- **Preserve the CI process environment**: Resolved shell variables are merged over the inherited environment so Windows retains `PATH` and can discover Docker.
- **Keep the fixture self-contained**: The suite writes a minimal `.devcontainer/devcontainer.json`, exposes the host mock server to the container, and removes both the fixture and labeled container during guaranteed teardown.
- **Scope of certificate coverage**: This smoke exercises startup, remote CLI installation, Agent Host startup, relay connection, authentication, and a complete turn. It does not simulate a private CA trusted only by the OS.

</details>

## Changes

- Add Agents Window automation for selecting Dev Container across dynamic control states.
- Probe for a reachable Linux Docker daemon, require it on Linux, and capability-skip elsewhere.
- Verify the assistant response, AHP transport, and remote session resource.
- Seed and validate a published fallback CLI for packaged branch builds.
- Forward the smoke-test token through remote Agent Host authentication.
- Clean up the generated configuration and labeled container even when app shutdown fails.

title: agentHost: Keep passive session opens from changing recency
body:
## Summary

- suppress the SDK `session.resume` event when Agent Host cold-opens an existing Copilot session
- keep observational session opens from advancing the persisted session modification time
- cover the resume configuration passed by the Copilot session launcher

Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/334501

## Problem

The Sessions view can show an old session as modified recently even though its last message was sent days ago.

For Copilot sessions, the displayed `updatedAt` ultimately comes from the SDK/runtime `modifiedTime`, which is based on the `events.jsonl` modification time. Cold-opening a session calls `resumeSession`; publishing a `session.resume` event can modify that journal, making a passive open look like recent user activity.

## Resolution

Agent Host now passes `suppressResumeEvent: true` when it resumes an existing session for display. This lets the runtime restore the live session without recording an observational resume event that changes recency.

## Dependency

**Blocked by https://github.com/github/copilot-agent-runtime/pull/18323. Do not merge until VS Code consumes a runtime release containing that change.**

The current runtime couples resume-event suppression with resume-state processing. Runtime PR #18323 separates those concerns so suppressed resumes still restore model/context and preserve orphan and pending-work semantics while avoiding journal writes, subscriber publication, and modified-time updates.

## Validation

- `npm run hygiene`
- `npm run typecheck-client`
- ESLint on both changed files
- `npm run transpile-client`
- `./scripts/test.sh --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts` — 46 passing

The full `npm run compile-client` currently reaches an unrelated `origin/main` declaration freshness failure where `DiffEditorViewMode` is regenerated into `src/vs/monaco.d.ts`; the client type-check and focused tests pass with dependencies restored from the current branch.

title: cli - allow --remove in remote cli pipe mode (fix microsoft/vscode-remote-release#11835)
body:
## Description

`code --remove` (introduced in #236580) is currently ignored in the remote CLI (pipe mode), e.g. when running `code --remove <folder>` from the integrated terminal of a WSL/SSH remote window:

```
Ignoring option 'remove': not supported for code.
```

The option is registered in `argv.ts`, and the pipe client already forwards `removeMode` (handled on the receiving side), but `remove` was never added to the `isSupportedForPipe` allowlist in `src/vs/server/node/server.cli.ts`, so `parseArgs` drops the option with the warning above.

This adds the missing case so that `--remove` is accepted in pipe mode, matching `--add`.

Fixes microsoft/vscode-remote-release#11835

## To test

1. Connect to a remote (WSL/SSH) and open the integrated terminal (pipe mode: `VSCODE_IPC_HOOK_CLI` set, `VSCODE_CLIENT_COMMAND` unset)
2. Run `code --add /some/folder`, then `code --remove /some/folder`
3. Before: `Ignoring option 'remove': not supported for code.` and the folder is not removed
4. After: no warning, the folder is removed from the last active window

title: Test: Customization migration hint
body:
Refs: #334303

- [x] anyOS @ulugbekna
- [x] anyOS @bamurtaugh

Complexity: 2

Authors: @aeschli


[Create Issue](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/new?template=blank&body=Testing+%23334500%0A%0A&assignees=aeschli)

---

Agent Host chat sessions can show a migration hint when customization files exist in locations that are not used by the active harness. The hint distinguishes workspace and user customizations and links directly to the relevant migration page.

## Test setup

Add the following to `settings.json`:

```json
"chat.customizations.migrationHint": "always",
"chat.customizations.promptMigration.enabled": true,
"chat.customizations.userDataMigration.enabled": true,
"chat.customizations.locationsMigration.enabled": true
```

Create valid customization files that are not supported by the active Agent Host harness. Include both workspace and user files, for example prompt files under the workspace and user prompt-file locations. Alternatively, configure unsupported workspace and user locations and add customization files there.

You can use https://github.com/aeschli/vscode-customization-migration-test as a starting point. It has the settings set as well as some workspace customizations that can be migrated.

Start a new Agent Host chat session using Copilot CLI or Claude and send a request.

## Verify hint content

- A customization migration hint is shown in the chat response when migratable files are discovered.
- The hint identifies workspace and user candidates separately, for example: `Found 2 workspace and 2 user customizations that are present but not used by Claude and could be migrated.`
- The counts include candidates from prompt files, user-data migrations, and configured-location migrations.
- When candidates exist in only one storage scope, the hint mentions only `workspace` or `user` as appropriate.
- Singular wording is used when exactly one customization can be migrated.
- The active harness name is shown in the message.
- No file migration hint is shown when all customization files are already supported by the active harness.
- Local, non-Agent-Host chat sessions do not show the hint.

## Verify Review customizations

- Select **Review customizations** in the hint.
- **Agent Customizations** opens for the originating Agent Host harness.
- Migration information is refreshed before navigation.
- The first applicable file-migration category is selected and rendered.
- Keyboard focus moves to the migration page's first actionable control.
- The displayed migration candidates and counts agree with the hint.

## Verify frequency

- With `chat.customizations.migrationHint` set to `always`, the hint is shown for every eligible request.
- With the setting set to `once`, the hint is shown only once in a chat session.
- Reloading a chat session in which the `once` hint was shown does not show it again.

title: Agents Window should respect git.enableCommitSigning
body:
When `git.enableCommitSigning` is enabled, commits created through the Source Control view are signed, but commits created by an agent in the Agents Window are not.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Configure a signing key in Git.
2. Enable `git.enableCommitSigning` in VS Code.
3. Create a commit through the Source Control view and confirm that it is signed.
4. Ask an agent in the Agents Window to create a commit.
5. Inspect the resulting commit signature.

## Actual behavior

The agent-created commit is unsigned. Agents invoke the Git CLI, where `user.signingKey` selects a key but does not enable signing unless `commit.gpgSign` is also configured or `git commit -S` is used. The VS Code `git.enableCommitSigning` setting is therefore not observed by the Agents Window.

This also affects agent-driven operations that rewrite commits, such as resolving conflicts through a rebase: the recreated commits remain unsigned.

## Expected behavior

Git operations initiated by the Agents Window should observe `git.enableCommitSigning`, so commits created or rewritten by an agent are signed consistently with commits created through the Source Control view.

Alternatively, the Agents Window should expose an equivalent signing policy and clearly explain how it relates to `git.enableCommitSigning` and Git\u2019s `commit.gpgSign` configuration.

Agent Merge is a new experimental controller in the Agents Window. Once enabled for a session, it watches that session's pull request and asks the agent to take care of the things that keep it from merging, such as failing CI, unresolved review comments, merge conflicts or a branch that fell behind. It can also merge the pull request once it is ready.

Once it is enabled, a run looks like this:

![Agent Merge conversation](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1cf17687-28a9-4d97-b940-bb6d6f394e40)

You need a GitHub repository you can push branches to and open pull requests in, ideally one with CI so you can produce a failing check.

- In the Agents Window, run a session that makes a change, then create a pull request for it from the **Changes** view.
- Once the pull request is open, the **Agent Merge** button appears in the Changes title bar. Use its dropdown to **Enable Agent Merge**, and **Configure Agent Merge** to pick which blockers it may handle (Address Reviews, Fix CI Failures, Resolve Conflicts and Behind Branches) and whether it may **Merge Pull Request** (On / Only if Agent Merge Made No Changes / Off).
- **Agent Merge Defaults** in the same dropdown opens the settings that all sessions follow.

## Test

- Enable Agent Merge for a session and verify the chat transcript explains what it will now do, and that the same happens when you change its configuration (the notice should make clear whether the change was for this session or for all sessions).

title: Agent Host: Use VS Code certificates for Dev Container CLI
body:
## Summary

Configure the bundled Dev Container CLI to use the certificates loaded by VS Code, including enterprise system certificates and user-provided `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`.

<details>
<summary>Session Context</summary>

Key decisions from the development session:

- **Do not force Node `--use-system-ca`**: That runtime switch would bypass VS Code certificate settings. The CLI instead receives a `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` bundle, matching the approach used by the Remote Containers extension.
- **Reuse VS Code certificate policy**: Certificate loading goes through `IRequestService.loadCertificates()`, while `http.systemCertificates` gates whether system certificates are added. The request service also honors `http.systemCertificatesNode`.
- **Preserve explicit environment configuration**: A valid existing `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` value wins and is passed through unchanged.
- **Use a VS Code-owned temporary namespace**: Generated content-addressed PEM files are cached under `<tmpDir>/vscode-dev-container`, rather than the Remote Containers extension-specific `vsch` directory.
- **Handle concurrent writers safely**: Each process writes a unique temporary file and atomically renames it to the certificate-content hash. A rename failure is accepted only when another process has already published the expected target.

</details>

## Changes

- Inject the shared-process request service into the Dev Container Agent Host launcher.
- Resolve the Dev Container CLI environment once per process.
- Preserve valid `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS` or generate a hashed PEM file from VS Code-loaded certificates.
- Add focused tests for explicit certificates, disabled system certificates, loaded system certificates, and the bundled CLI.

## Validation

- 3 focused unit tests passing
- ESLint
- Client typecheck
- Hygiene and diff checks

Refs #317380

title: Alt keyup is missed while a webview editor has focus, silently turning a tab's Close button into "Close Other Editors"

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body: Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Yes - VS Code Version: 1.136.1 (commit a44adf7f53e00964ab890f9f8758a334f1fc15bc) - OS Version: Windows_NT x64 10.0.26200 ## Steps to reproduce 1. Open several editor tabs. 2. **Give focus to a webview-backed editor** (see Scope). This is required — the bug does not occur when a normal text editor has focus. 3. Focus a different application. 4. Hold Alt and press Tab repeatedly to cycle back to the VS Code window. Keep Alt held for roughly a second after the switcher lands on VS Code, then release it. 5. Without pressing any key, hover a tab's close button. 6. The button's glyph changes and the tooltip reads **"Close Others (Alt+Click)"**. 7. Clicking it closes every other editor. Normal state — plain `×` close buttons: After the Alt+Tab, with no key pressed — the glyph has changed and the tooltip offers Close Others: Note that in the second image no modifier key is being held. The window simply still believes one is. ## Scope The focused-editor type is the discriminator, confirmed by testing: - Focus in a **normal text editor** — no repro. The Alt keyup is seen and the close button stays a plain Close. - Focus in a **webview-backed editor** — reproduces every time. - Confirmed with the **built-in Markdown preview** (open a `.md` file, Ctrl+K V, click into the preview pane), so this needs no extension. It was originally found with a third-party webview editor, and both behave identically. A second window launched with `--disable-extensions`, containing only text editors, did not reproduce — consistent with the focused-editor type being the discriminator rather than any extension. The likely mechanism: while focus is inside the webview's iframe, the Alt keyup is not propagated to the workbench's modifier tracking, so the workbench keeps believing Alt is held. Because nothing re-syncs modifier state when the window gains focus, the stale state then survives indefinitely. The long Alt hold matters: the Alt keyup is delivered to the window switcher after VS Code has already taken focus, so VS Code sees the modifier as still held. **The latched state is cleared only by keyboard input — never by a focus change.** With the window in this state, clicking away to another application via the taskbar and then clicking back leaves the close button still in Close Other Editors mode. Pressing any key clears it immediately. (This also makes it awkward to inspect: opening Developer Tools via Ctrl+Shift+I clears the state through the keypress itself. Inspecting requires freezing the UI first, e.g. `setTimeout(() => { debugger }, 5000)` from the console, then hovering during the delay.) The persistence across a blur/focus cycle suggests the window's modifier state is never re-synced when it gains focus. ## Expected Once Alt is physically released, VS Code should not treat it as held. The tab close button should be a plain **Close**. ## Actual The close button remains in **Close Other Editors** mode for an arbitrary period after focus, with no indication other than a hover tooltip. A single click destroys the whole editor group except one tab. ## Why this is more than a cosmetic modifier glitch The Alt-latch on Windows focus switches is long-standing and was previously harmless in the tab bar, because the close button had no alternate action. The affordance added in **1.134** ("Close other editors from a tab", #328975) gave it one, which turns a pre-existing, invisible platform condition into a destructive action: - Closing one tab is among the highest-frequency mouse actions in the editor, and Alt+Tab is among the most common ways to return to the window. The two compose directly. - There is no signal at click time. The changed glyph and tooltip only appear on hover, and closing a tab is muscle memory — nobody hovers and reads first. - The outcome is hard to undo. **Reopen Closed Editor** is the only recourse, and only until the window is reloaded. For webview-backed tabs (chat/agent sessions, notebooks, custom editors) the loss is more disruptive than for text editors. - There is no way to opt out of just this behaviour. The only workaround is `"workbench.editor.tabActionCloseVisibility": false`, which removes the close button entirely. This was hit as an actual data-loss event: a set of long-running agent-session tabs was wiped by one click on a `×` after an Alt+Tab, on the same day the client moved onto 1.134. ## Possible mitigations Any one of these would be sufficient: 1. Reset modifier state on window blur/focus, and only honour Alt if a keydown was received by the window *after* it gained focus. There is precedent: #241190 (Ctrl not registered right after an Alt+Tab focus switch) was fixed this way in the February 2025 milestone. 2. Require the modifier to be pressed while the pointer is already over the tab bar, rather than accepting an ambient modifier state. 3. Add a setting to disable the alternate close action. 4. Route the alternate action through the existing confirmation for closing multiple editors. ## Note on history This was originally proposed in #193357 (Sept 2023) and closed as `*out-of-scope`; it shipped later via #328975. The latched-modifier case does not appear to have been considered in either thread.

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! bug_report_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- 🕮 Read our guide about submitting issues: https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/Submitting-Bugs-and-Suggestions -->

<!-- 🔧 Launch with `code --disable-extensions` to check. -->
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: No / not applicable. The reproducer depends on the built-in Agent Host / Codex changed-files workflow, so disabling that functionality removes the affected code path rather than meaningfully testing it.

<!-- 🪓 If you answered No above, use 'Help: Start Extension Bisect' from Command Palette to try to identify the cause. -->
<!-- 📣 Issues caused by an extension need to be reported directly to the extension publisher. The 'Help > Report Issue' dialog can assist with this. -->
- VS Code Version: 1.136.1, commit `a44adf7f53e00964ab890f9f8758a334f1fc15bc`
- OS Version: Windows 11 x64 (`Windows_NT 10.0.26200`)
- Remote environment: Linux / Ubuntu via VS Code Remote-SSH
- Remote Agent Host / Codex package: `0.146.0`

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Run VS Code on Windows.
2. Connect to a Linux machine using Remote-SSH.
3. Open a folder on the remote machine.
4. Start a Codex / Agent Host chat session.
5. Ask the agent to make a small edit to an existing file in the remote workspace.
6. Wait for the response containing the `1 file changed` summary.
7. Click the changed file in that summary.

### Actual result

The remote POSIX file path is treated as a local Windows `file:` resource.

For example, the real remote file:

    /var/www/example/web/project/config.php

is displayed / opened on the Windows side as:

    \var\www\example\web\project\config.php

and VS Code fails with an error similar to:

    Unable to read file '\var\www\example\web\project\config.php'
    (Error: Unable to resolve nonexistent file '\var\www\example\web\project\config.php')

The file itself exists and opens normally through the Remote-SSH workspace.

The correct workspace resource is of the form:

    vscode-remote://ssh-remote+my-host/var/www/example/web/project/config.php

### Expected result

Clicking the changed file should open its diff using the Remote-SSH filesystem provider.

The modified side should resolve to the remote workspace resource instead of being interpreted as a local Windows filesystem path.

### Investigation

I traced the issue to the Agent Host URI mapping.

In:

`src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostUri.ts`

the current implementation contains:

    function wrapAgentHostUri(originalUri: URI, connectionAuthority: string, contentRef: boolean): URI {
        if (connectionAuthority === 'local' && originalUri.scheme === Schemas.file) {
            return originalUri;
        }

        // ...
    }

The same source also documents the assumption behind the `local` authority:

    /**
     * Authority of the in-process agent host. It always runs on the same
     * machine — and therefore the same operating system — as the client.
     */
    export const LOCAL_AGENT_HOST_AUTHORITY = 'local';

In this Remote-SSH scenario, however, a POSIX URI such as:

    file:///var/www/example/web/project/config.php

produced by the Agent Host eventually reaches the Windows renderer unchanged.

Windows then interprets it as a local filesystem resource and converts it to:

    \var\www\example\web\project\config.php

The per-response changed-files provider also constructs the modified resource through `toAgentHostUri(...)`.

### Git / snapshot side is not the cause

I also verified the original side of the diff.

The `git-blob:` resource used for the original version is readable. A `resourceRead` request succeeds and returns the expected content.

A subsequent `createResourceWatch` request against the immutable `git-blob:` resource may fail with `Resource not found`, but this is separate from the modified-file failure.

The underlying Git commit, repository-relative path, and `git show <commit>:<path>` lookup all work correctly.

### Working diagnostic workaround

I tested a local modification to the compiled VS Code workbench bundle.

For the affected remote workspace path only, instead of returning the raw `file:` URI, I mapped it to the active Remote-SSH resource:

    URI.from({
        scheme: "vscode-remote",
        authority: "ssh-remote+my-host",
        path: originalUri.path,
        query: originalUri.query,
        fragment: originalUri.fragment
    })

Before this change:

    file:///var/www/example/web/project/config.php
        ->
    \var\www\example\web\project\config.php
        ->
    Unable to resolve nonexistent file

After this change and a full VS Code restart:

    vscode-remote://ssh-remote+my-host/var/www/example/web/project/config.php
        ->
    diff opens correctly

No other change was required.

This is only a diagnostic workaround, not a proposed final architectural fix. The proper fix likely needs to map Agent Host `file:` resources back into the current Remote-SSH client resource space instead of assuming that `connectionAuthority === "local"` means the renderer can directly access the same filesystem.

### Relevant source paths

The affected changed-file summary is backed by the Agent Host response-file changes provider, which eventually maps the modified file through `toAgentHostUri(...)`.

Relevant source files include:

    src/vs/platform/agentHost/common/agentHostUri.ts
    src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/agentSessions/agentHost/agentHostResponseFileChanges.ts
    src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/chatChangesSummaryPart.ts

### Related issue

There is an existing OpenAI Codex issue with a very similar user-visible failure in a Windows -> Remote-SSH -> Linux setup:

https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/36323

That report describes changed-file preview information working, while opening/reviewing the diff fails.

### Additional notes

The issue reproduces with a newly created Codex edit, so it is not caused by stale session data.

The remote file can be opened normally from Explorer and from the editor when accessed through its `vscode-remote://` resource.

The failure is specifically in the changed-file / diff flow when a remote Linux `file:` URI reaches the Windows renderer as a plain local file URI.

Users can migrate agents, instructions, and skills from custom locations that are not supported by the active agent harness. Successfully migrated customizations are moved into source folders provided by that harness, and location settings that become unused can optionally be cleared.

```json
"chat.modeFilesLocations": { ".custom/modes": true },

```

Create valid customization files in the configured folders, for example:

- `.custom/agents/test.agent.md`
- `.custom/modes/test.chatmode.md`
- `.custom/instructions/test.instructions.md`
- `.custom/skills/test-skill/SKILL.md`
- 
You can use https://github.com/aeschli/vscode-customization-migration-test as a starting point. It has the settings set as well as some workspace customizations that can be migrated.

Open **Agent Customizations** with an agent-host harness active whose supported source folders differ from these configured locations.

## Verify discovery and navigation

- The overview page shows the **Migrate Custom Locations** card when customizations exist in unsupported configured locations.
- The sidebar shows **Migrate Custom Locations** with the correct candidate count.
- Settings that retain their default value are not listed in the migration guidance.
- Each listed setting is a link that opens the Settings editor filtered to that setting.
- Resetting all relevant settings to their defaults hides the migration card and sidebar shortcut.
- If the currently open migration page becomes unavailable after resetting the settings, the editor returns to the overview page.

## Verify the migration page

- Customizations are grouped under **Agents**, **Instructions**, and **Skills** as applicable.
- Each group is collapsible, has a select-all checkbox, and supports selecting individual files.
- Selecting the content area of a file row opens it in the embedded editor.
- Returning from the embedded editor returns to **Migrate Custom Locations**.
- The migration button and selected-item count update as the selection changes.
- Migration destinations are supported source folders supplied by the active harness.
- If several compatible destination folders are available, a destination picker is shown.

## Verify unused-setting cleanup

- A collapsible **Settings** group is shown after the customization groups.
- **Clear unused location settings** is selected by default.
- The option remains selected and enabled when only some files are selected.
- After a successful partial migration:
  - settings no longer needed by any remaining customization are cleared;
  - settings still needed by unselected customizations remain unchanged.
- Agent and legacy mode location settings remain while any agent customization is left unmigrated.
- After successfully migrating all files, all applicable unused location settings are cleared.
- Deselecting **Clear unused location settings** leaves every setting unchanged.
- A setting is not cleared if its selected customizations fail to migrate.

## Verify migration results

- Starting migration opens a confirmation dialog.
- The confirmation allows retaining or deleting the original files.
- Successfully migrated agents, instructions, and skills preserve their names and content.
- Skills preserve their directory structure and supporting files.
- When originals are deleted:
  - the migration inventory refreshes;
  - the editor navigates to the corresponding customization section;
  - a migrated customization is revealed and selected.
- Per-file failures are reported without presenting the overall migration as fully successful.

title: Copilot Git remote fallback fails for linked worktrees
body:
## Symptom

Recent Code Insiders sessions repeatedly log an error when Copilot tries to discover repository remotes for agent-created linked worktrees:

```text
2026-09-02 09:04:43.837 [error] [GitServiceImpl][getRepositoryFetchUrls] Failed to read remotes from .git/config: Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory, open '<worktree>/.git/config'
```

```text
2026-09-03 09:03:09.012 [error] [GitServiceImpl][getRepositoryFetchUrls] Failed to read remotes from .git/config: Error: ENOTDIR: not a directory, open '<worktree>/.git/config'
```

## Brief analysis

The fallback in `extensions/copilot/src/platform/git/vscode-node/gitServiceImpl.ts#getRepositoryFetchUrls` assumes the repository config is always at `<repositoryRoot>/.git/config`.

For a linked Git worktree, `.git` is a file containing a `gitdir:` pointer, for example:

```text
gitdir: <main-repository>/.git/worktrees/<worktree-name>
```

That administrative directory normally contains a `commondir` file (commonly `../..`) pointing to the shared Git directory where `config` lives. Reading `.git/config` therefore fails with `ENOTDIR`.

The method catches the error and returns `undefined`, so callers such as content-exclusion repository discovery cannot identify the worktree's remotes through this fallback. The fallback should resolve `gitdir` and optional `commondir` metadata before reading the config, while preserving the existing regular-repository path.

Since updating to the 1.136 line, all icons contributed by extensions that run
on the **remote** side fail to load in a Remote-SSH window. The activity bar
buttons and the editor tab icons are present and fully clickable, but render as
empty/grey squares. Extension functionality is unaffected — only the images are
missing.

dies with `net::ERR_FAILED`. Built-in codicons (Explorer, Search, Source
Control, Run and Debug, Extensions, Testing) are unaffected, since they come
from a font bundled in the client.

This looks like a regression of the same family as #319834 ("Extension
icons/fonts blocked by CORS policy on vscode-managed-remote-resource"), which
was reported against 1.123.0 and fixed in the 1.124.0 milestone. The console
wording differs — `net::ERR_FAILED` here, `blocked by CORS policy` there — so
I cannot claim it is the identical root cause, only the identical symptom on
the identical scheme.

### Version / environment

- VS Code: **1.136.1**, commit `a44adf7f53e00964ab890f9f8758a334f1fc15bc`, x64
- Client OS: Linux x64, installed from the official `.deb`
- Remote OS: Linux x64 (Ubuntu, kernel 6.8)

| version | activity bar icons of remote extensions |
|---|---|
| 1.135.0 | OK |
| 1.136.0 | broken |
| 1.136.1 | broken |

The affected machine ran 1.135.0 from 25 Aug 2026 with no problem; the icons
disappeared with the 1.136 line.

### Steps to reproduce

1. Connect to a remote host with Remote-SSH.
2. Install on the **remote** side any extension that contributes an activity
   bar view container with an SVG/PNG icon (e.g. `ms-python.python`).
3. Reload the window.

**Expected:** the extension icon is drawn in the activity bar.
**Actual:** the button is present and clickable, but the icon area is blank.

Paths anonymised; `USER` and `HOST` replace the real values.

    ms-python.vscode-python-envs-1.36.0-linux-x64/files/logo.svg

The `claude-logo.svg` request repeats about a dozen times per window load.

title: Keep auto experiment defaults applied when assignments are refetched
body:
This stops experiment-driven setting defaults from being dropped and re-applied whenever assignments are refetched, which made the workbench visibly blink between the classic and Modern UI layouts shortly after startup.

### Changes

- `ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution` now keeps an experiment default that is already registered with the same resolved value, instead of re-evaluating it and deregistering it.
- This fixes an oscillation: the configuration registry mutates `property.default` to reflect registered default overrides, so once an `auto` experiment was applied, the next resolution compared the treatment against itself, concluded it matched the default, and removed the override. `WorkbenchAssignmentService` fires `onDidRefetchAssignments` shortly after the initial assignment fetch, so this happened during startup — `workbench.experimental.modernUI` flipped back to `false`, `updateFloatingPanels()` stripped the `modern-ui` classes, and a later refetch flipped it back.
- `shouldOverride` is deliberately left unchanged. Comparing against the schema-authored default instead would silently drop a control-arm assignment whenever another non-experiment `configurationDefaults` override exists for the same key, and would make `preventExperimentOverride` redundant.
- Startup-mode latching, the `preventExperimentOverride` guard, the Agents window `agentsWindow.default` comparison, and removal when a treatment resolves to `undefined` are all unaffected.
- Added regression coverage for an auto experiment surviving a refetch, and for a control-arm value still winning over an unrelated default override.

### Validation

- `./scripts/test.sh --grep "Configuration|Sessions ConfigurationService|WorkspaceService"` — 770 passing, 7 pending.
- Both new tests were confirmed to fail against the unmodified source and pass with the fix. The guard test's initial-resolution assertion is identical before and after, confirming the existing override semantics are preserved.

Fixes microsoft/vscode#334427

When using Codex through Agent Host, the permissions selector currently offers only Default Permissions, Auto-Review, and Full Access. Each preset expands to explicit approval, sandbox, and reviewer values, so users cannot choose the permissions they already maintain in Codex config.toml.

Agent Host should offer a Custom permissions option that uses Codex's effective configuration:

- New threads should avoid overriding the configured permission values.
- Subsequent turns, resumed sessions, and forks should use the current effective permission configuration instead of retaining stale thread values.
- Both legacy approval_policy / sandbox_mode configuration and named default_permissions profiles should be supported.
- Existing Default Permissions, Auto-Review, and Full Access behavior should remain unchanged.

Only the effective permission projection should be passed to thread operations. Other configuration, including credentials and MCP server definitions, should continue to be owned and loaded by Codex.

This would let Agent Host users share the same permission policy they use with the Codex CLI and app without duplicating it in every VS Code session.

title: Copilot Chat: switching a session to autopilot mid-conversation injects task_complete instructions into the middle of the system prompt, invalidating prefix cache for third-party (chatProvider) models

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Issues that have not been triaged in an appropriate amount of time

body:
### Summary When a chat session switches its permission level to **autopilot** mid-conversation, Copilot Chat injects the autopilot `task_complete` instruction **into the middle of the single system message**. For custom language model providers (via the `chatProvider` proposed API) that rely on automatic **prefix caching** (DeepSeek and other OpenAI-compatible endpoints, which have no cache-breakpoint concept), every token after the injection point misses the cache and the full turn is billed at full price. The extension (`oai-compatible-copilot` style third-party providers) only forwards `messages` as received — it cannot reorder or split the merged system message — so this is a host-side rendering concern. ### Reproduction 1. Start an agent-mode chat in VS Code (default/assisted permission level). 2. Run a few turns so the backend has a large cached prefix (e.g. ~360k input tokens, >99% cache hits). 3. Mid-session, switch the conversation to **autopilot** (auto-approve) and send the next request. 4. Observe the upstream `cached_tokens` drop from ~99.9% of input to ~1%. Both requests in step 2 and 3 carry the **same routing session** (same backend pod); only the request payload changes. ### Evidence from two captured requests (same conversation, 6 minutes apart) | field | before (interactive) | after (switched to autopilot) | |---|---|---| | tools count | 80 (no `task_complete`) | 81 (**+ `task_complete`**) | | system contains autopilot instruction | no | **yes, inserted at char 20,407** (306 chars) | | upstream `usage.input_tokens` | 359,410 | 325,827 | | upstream `cached_tokens` | **359,296 (99.9%)** | **3,328 (~1%)** | The exact inserted text is the autopilot block: > When you have fully completed the task, call the task_complete tool to signal that you are done. > IMPORTANT: Before calling task_complete, you MUST provide a brief text summary of what was accomplished in your message. The task is not complete until both the summary and the task_complete call are present. ### Root cause (source pointers) 1. **`extensions/copilot/src/extension/intents/node/agentIntent.ts:289`** — `task_complete` is only enabled when `request.permissionLevel === 'autopilot'`. 2. **`extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/agent/agentPrompt.tsx:130, 140-143`** — the same flag gates a `` block that is rendered as part of `baseInstructions`, i.e. *inside the system section*, between the static identity/custom-instruction blocks and the user context: ```tsx const isAutopilot = this.props.promptContext.request?.permissionLevel === 'autopilot'; ... {isAutopilot && When you have fully completed the task, call the task_complete tool to signal that you are done.
IMPORTANT: Before calling task_complete, you MUST provide a brief text summary of what was accomplished in your message. The task is not complete until both the summary and the task_complete call are present. } ``` 3. **`extensions/copilot/src/extension/prompts/node/base/promptRenderer.ts:107-131`** — consecutive system messages are collapsed into the single `messages[0]` text by concatenation, so that conditional block ends up embedded in the *middle* of the system prompt. On the observed request it landed at character ~20,407 of ~21,169, with the rest of the system text and the whole conversation history following after it. 4. Notably, the host already implements a protection against exactly this class of problem but does not cover these conditional blocks — **`agentPrompt.tsx:242-299` (`getOrFreezeCustomizationsIndex`)** snapshots the ``/``/`` customizations index on the first turn and reuses it, moving per-turn changes into a `drift` block rendered in the *latest user message*, explicitly "to stop per-turn churn … from invalidating the system prompt cache". The `isAutopilot` / `isVoiceModeInput` / `templateVariablesContext` conditional system blocks are outside that mechanism. ### Suggested fix Render request-scoped, potentially *changing* conditional instructions (autopilot `task_complete`, voice-mode, template variables) the same way `drift` is handled — append them to the **latest user message** (or a trailing system block after conversation history) rather than merging them into the middle of the leading system prompt. Since these blocks only toggle when the session mode changes (entering/exiting autopilot), doing so keeps the system prefix byte-stable across turns and restores prefix-cache hits for OpenAI-compatible providers that lack `cache_control` breakpoints. Alternative/complementary: when the conditional block *does* change, accept the one-time cache miss but keep the change at the very tail of the prompt (after history), limiting invalidation to the appended delta instead of the entire 300k+ token history. ### Environment - VS Code: 1.136.0 (extension host forwards host-assembled `messages` unchanged to third-party providers via `chatProvider` proposed API) - Copilot Chat: built-in (lockstep release) - Model endpoint: DeepSeek v4 flash via an OpenAI-compatible gateway (`oai-compatible-copilot/0.4.2` extension acting as `LanguageModelChatProvider`) - All observations made 2026-09-04

title: Window reload causes a visible blink/layout shift between classic and Modern UI layouts

labels.name: insiders-released
labels.description: Patch has been released in VS Code Insiders

body:
## Summary

When reloading the window (`Developer: Reload Window`, or after certain settings/extension changes that trigger a reload), the workbench visibly blinks and shifts layout right after startup: it briefly renders with one layout (Modern UI floating panels on/off), then a moment later flips to the other layout. This looks like the window "shifts into Modern UX, then shifts back" within a fraction of a second.

## Suspected root cause

`workbench.experimental.modernUI` is registered as an **auto experiment** setting:

```ts
// src/vs/workbench/browser/workbench.contribution.ts
[LayoutSettings.MODERN_UI]: {
    'type': 'boolean',
    'default': false,
    ...
    experiment: { mode: 'auto' },
},
```

Its *effective* default value is not resolved synchronously at startup. `ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution` (`src/vs/workbench/services/configuration/browser/configurationService.ts`) asynchronously calls `IWorkbenchAssignmentService.getTreatment('config.workbench.experimental.modernUI')` and, once the ExP treatment resolves, registers a configuration *default override* and fires a `deltaConfiguration`. Only then does `Workbench#registerLayoutListeners` see `affectsConfiguration(LayoutSettings.MODERN_UI)` and call `updateFloatingPanels()` (`src/vs/workbench/browser/layout.ts`), which toggles the `modern-ui` / `modern-ui-compact` classes on the workbench container and re-lays out the floating side/panel parts.

Meanwhile, the *splash screen* that is painted before any JS/workbench code runs is built from the **previous session's** persisted layout info:

```ts
// src/vs/workbench/contrib/splash/browser/partsSplash.ts
layoutInfo: !this._shouldSaveLayoutInfo() ? undefined : {
    ...
    modernUI: this._layoutService.isFloatingPanelsEnabled(),
    ...
}
```

which is read back in the pre-load splash renderer:

```ts
// src/vs/code/electron-browser/workbench/workbench.ts
const modernUI = layoutInfo.modernUI === true;
```

So the timeline on reload is:
1. Native splash paints instantly using the **cached** `modernUI` value from the last session (e.g. `true`, once the user was already bucketed into the experiment).
2. The real workbench boots with the configuration service's **built-in default** (`false`), since the experiment override hasn't been (re-)applied yet this session → the container's `modern-ui` classes are removed → visible shift *out of* Modern UI.
3. Shortly after, `ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution` resolves the ExP treatment and re-applies the override → `updateFloatingPanels()` runs again → the classes are re-added → visible shift *back into* Modern UI.

This produces the blink/layout-shift reported when reloading the window, and would also explain why it doesn't reproduce every time (depends on how fast the assignment/treatment fetch resolves relative to first layout).

## Steps to reproduce

1. Be enrolled (or use a setting override) so that `workbench.experimental.modernUI` is expected to end up `true` via experimentation.
2. Run `Developer: Reload Window`.
3. Observe the workbench briefly flash between the classic and Modern UI floating-panel layouts right after the window becomes visible.

## Possible fixes to investigate

- Persist the *resolved* experiment value (not just the last computed `isFloatingPanelsEnabled()`) and short-circuit `ConfigurationDefaultOverridesContribution` to apply that cached value synchronously before the first layout/render, only reconciling with the live ExP treatment afterwards (similar in spirit to how the splash screen already caches other layout info).
- Alternatively, delay first layout/paint of the affected parts until the `auto` experiment settings have resolved at least once, when a cached prior value exists.

## Environment

Reported via internal Slack discussion; occurs during normal window reloads (`Developer: Reload Window`) on Insiders builds with `workbench.experimental.modernUI` under experimentation.

_Created from a [Slack conversation](https://vscodeteam.slack.com/archives/C1C2M1KEZ/p1788492282533439?thread_ts=1788492282.533439&cid=C1C2M1KEZ)._

Type: Bug ### Environment - VS Code: 1.136.1 - GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.64.1 - OS: Windows - Provider: LM Studio through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint - Original registered model: `prism-ml/bonsai-27b` - Model subsequently loaded by LM Studio: `google/gemma-4-12b-qat` - Custom agent/subagent workflow using VS Code custom agents ### Steps to reproduce 1. Configure an LM Studio OpenAI-compatible model in VS Code/Copilot Chat. 2. Start a Copilot chat while LM Studio is serving `prism-ml/bonsai-27b`. 3. Send a request that invokes a custom agent or subagent. 4. In LM Studio, switch the loaded model to `google/gemma-4-12b-qat`. 5. Reuse the existing Copilot chat. 6. Send another request that invokes a custom agent or subagent. 7. Compare the Copilot debug logs with the LM Studio server logs. ### Actual behavior LM Studio reports that all requests after the switch were processed by `google/gemma-4-12b-qat`. title: BYOK Custom Endpoint: allow explicit Responses API tool search capability in chatLanguageModels.json

body:
<!-- ⚠️⚠️ Do Not Delete This! feature_request_template ⚠️⚠️ -->
<!-- Please read our Rules of Conduct: https://opensource.microsoft.com/codeofconduct/ -->
<!-- Please search existing issues to avoid creating duplicates. -->

<!-- Describe the feature you'd like. -->
## Feature request

Allow BYOK models configured with the `customendpoint` provider and `apiType: "responses"` to explicitly opt into VS Code's existing client-executed Responses API tool search through `chatLanguageModels.json`.

## Problem

VS Code already has the Responses API tool-search implementation in place. In `extensions/copilot/src/platform/endpoint/node/responsesApi.ts`, tool search is enabled when `endpoint.supportsToolSearch` is true and the tool-search tool is available. The request is then shaped as the Responses API client-executed tool-search protocol (`{ type: "tool_search", execution: "client" }`), with deferred tools loaded through `tool_search_call` / `tool_search_output`.

However, `customendpoint` model configuration currently has no way to explicitly set that capability:

* `_CustomEndpointModelConfig` exposes fields such as `toolCalling`, `vision`, `thinking`, `adaptiveThinking`, and `supportsReasoningEffort`, but no tool-search capability.
* `BYOKModelCapabilities` / `resolveModelInfo()` do not populate `capabilities.supports.tool_search` from user configuration.
* `ChatEndpoint` already supports explicit metadata via `modelMetadata.capabilities.supports.tool_search`, but when it is absent it falls back to `modelSupportsToolSearch(this)`, which relies on known model IDs/families.

That fallback is useful for built-in/known models, but it is not a reliable authority for custom endpoints. A custom endpoint can proxy or rename a model, expose a future compatible model, or implement the Responses API tool-search protocol independently of a model ID that VS Code recognizes.

There is also `chat.modelCapabilityOverrides`, but that aliases the model family for capability routing in general. Using it just to enable tool search can unintentionally opt the custom model into other family-based behavior, so it is not a good replacement for a fine-grained capability flag.

## Proposed behavior

Add an optional per-model boolean in `chatLanguageModels.json`, for example:

```json
[
  {
    "vendor": "customendpoint",
    "apiKey": "${input:chat.lm.secret.example}",
    "models": [
      {
        "id": "my-responses-model",
        "name": "My Responses Model",
        "url": "https://example.com/v1/responses",
        "apiType": "responses",
        "toolCalling": true,
        "toolSearch": true,
        "vision": false,
        "maxInputTokens": 200000,
        "maxOutputTokens": 32000
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

Suggested semantics:

* `"toolSearch": true`: explicitly enable the existing tool-search path.
* `"toolSearch": false`: explicitly disable it, even if the model ID/family would otherwise match VS Code's built-in heuristic.
* omitted: preserve the current behavior and fall back to `modelSupportsToolSearch(...)`.

The three-state behavior fits the current `ChatEndpoint` logic because it already uses:

```ts
modelMetadata.capabilities.supports.tool_search ?? modelSupportsToolSearch(this)
```

## Possible implementation

The existing Responses API implementation should not need substantial changes. This could mainly be capability plumbing:

1. Add `toolSearch?: boolean` to `_CustomEndpointModelConfig`.
2. Add a corresponding optional field to `BYOKModelCapabilities`.
3. In `resolveModelInfo()`, preserve the optional value as `capabilities.supports.tool_search` rather than coercing it to `false`, so omission still falls back to the existing heuristic.
4. Pass the configured value through `CustomEndpointBYOKModelProvider.createOpenAIEndPoint()`.
5. Add the property to the `chatLanguageModels.json` schema in `extensions/copilot/package.json`.

For example:

```ts
tool_search: knownModelInfo?.toolSearch
```

rather than:

```ts
tool_search: !!knownModelInfo?.toolSearch
```

so `undefined` remains distinguishable from an explicit `false`.

## Why explicit configuration is preferable here

For a custom endpoint, VS Code cannot reliably determine support from the model name alone. The endpoint owner/user is in a better position to know whether the configured Responses API implementation accepts and correctly handles client-executed `tool_search`.

An explicit opt-in also avoids accidentally sending the special tool-search protocol to incompatible OpenAI-compatible endpoints, while still allowing proxies and custom/future models that do support it to use VS Code's existing tool deferral implementation.

I searched the existing VS Code issues for `tool_search`, BYOK, custom endpoint, and Responses API and did not find an issue covering this explicit custom-endpoint capability switch.

title: Agent host: a slash command is never executed when the turn carries host context
body:
### Summary

In the agent chat, a slash command is offered by completion and submits normally, but is never executed. The model receives the raw text and answers from its own knowledge, so it reads as the command being missing rather than broken.

### Cause

The prompt composer returns the user's text as the first content block and then appends host-composed context after it: attachment representations, read-only snapshot notes, and the reference reminder. The Claude CLI only treats a message as a slash command when its content is a **single** text block. Any turn carrying context therefore silently stops being a command.

### Reproduction

Run against the SDK the host spawns, same session and options, varying only the shape of `message.content`:

| `content` | result |
|---|---|
| `"/list-agents"` (string) | expands: `No subagents, teammates or other Claude sessions.` |
| `"/list-agents\n\n<context>...</context>"` (string) | expands |
| `[{type:"text",text:"/list-agents"}]` | expands |
| `[{type:"text",text:"/list-agents\n\n<context>...</context>"}]` | expands |
| `[{type:"text",text:"/list-agents"},{type:"text",text:"<context>...</context>"}]` | **does not expand** |

In the failing case the model replies with invented prose, `No agents are currently running. You can spawn a new agent using the Agent tool...`, instead of the command's real output.

The discriminator is the **number of text blocks**, not the presence of context.

### Evidence from a real session

- The SDK's `system/init` message advertises 46 `slash_commands` including `code-review`, so discovery is correct and completion is right to offer it.
- A transcript entry for a real user message beginning `/code-review` records its `content` as an array of two text blocks, which is the failing shape above.
- An unknown command is reported explicitly by the CLI (`Unknown command: /nope`), so the failure is not a lookup miss. The message simply never reaches command handling.

### Impact

Every slash command in the agent chat is affected whenever the turn carries an attachment or context. Because completion still lists the command, it presents as the command not existing.

### Suggested fix

Merge the appended text blocks into the first when the message is a slash command. The table above shows a single text block with the context appended inline still expands, so no context has to be dropped, and non-text blocks such as images can follow unchanged.

*AI disclosure: this issue and the related investigation were written with the assistance of AI.*

title: Copilot Agent repeatedly invokes disabled task_complete, causing tool loop and Extension Host CPU/RAM growth

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Issues that have not been triaged in an appropriate amount of time

body:
## Type of issue

Performance / Agent mode regression

## Environment

- VS Code: 1.136.1 (Remote Linux server build `a44adf7f53e00964ab890f9f8758a334f1fc15bc`)
- GitHub Copilot Chat: 0.64.1
- Remote OS: Linux
- Previous server build contained Copilot Chat 0.64.0

## Description

After the update to Copilot Chat 0.64.1, Agent mode became progressively slower and eventually stopped working. The Agent repeatedly adds the internal `task_complete` tool in autopilot mode even though that tool is disabled/unavailable. The invocation fails, but the Agent then adds the same tool again and continues the tool loop.

This correlates with sustained Extension Host CPU usage and large memory growth. In two affected VS Code windows, the Extension Host processes reached approximately:

- 40% CPU and 5.7 GB RSS
- 22% CPU and 2.0 GB RSS

The separate MCP server used by the workspace remained responsive and used only about 80 MB RSS, so the resource growth appears to be inside the Extension Host/Copilot Agent runtime.

## Relevant log sequence

```text
[ToolCallingLoop] Added task_complete tool for autopilot mode
Error from tool task_complete ...: Tool task_complete is currently disabled by the user, and cannot be called.
[ToolCallingLoop] Added task_complete tool for autopilot mode
[ToolCallingLoop] Autopilot: task_complete found in history, stopping
```

This sequence occurred repeatedly after validation commands. The same session also logged intermittent errors that may indicate related compatibility problems:

```text
PendingMigrationError: navigator is now a global in nodejs
Error compiling input schema for tool run_in_terminal: strict mode: unknown keyword: "enumDescriptions"
[ChatWebSocketManager] Error for conversation ... turn ...
```

A long-running session eventually also reached the 12,288 prompt-token limit, but the CPU/RAM growth and repeated completion-tool failures started before that limit error.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Use VS Code 1.136.1 with Copilot Chat 0.64.1 on a Remote Linux workspace.
2. Start an Agent mode task that performs edits and validation commands.
3. Use autopilot while `task_complete` is disabled or unavailable.
4. Let the Agent reach its completion/validation phase.
5. Observe repeated `Added task_complete tool` and disabled-tool errors in the Copilot Chat output.
6. Observe the Extension Host CPU and RSS continue to grow; Agent responses become progressively slower and may stop progressing.

## Expected behavior

If `task_complete` is disabled or unavailable, autopilot should not add or invoke it. A failed completion-tool invocation should terminate cleanly or fall back once, without re-entering a repeated tool loop. CPU and memory should return to idle levels after the turn completes.

## Actual behavior

The disabled completion tool is repeatedly re-added/invoked across completion attempts. The Agent becomes increasingly slow while the Extension Host retains high CPU usage and multiple gigabytes of memory. Reloading the window is required to recover.

## Regression notes

The behavior was first observed immediately after the server update from the build containing Copilot Chat 0.64.0 to the build containing 0.64.1. I have not yet performed a controlled downgrade comparison.

Related high-resource reports such as microsoft/vscode-copilot-release#12875, #11468, and #4985 do not include this disabled-`task_complete` loop.

title: macOS Vietnamese Telex IME causes line/cursor jump in integrated terminal (not editor, not Terminal.app)

labels.name: stale
labels.description: Issues that have not been triaged in an appropriate amount of time

labels.name: new release
labels.description: Issues found in a recent release of VS Code

body:
Does this issue occur when all extensions are disabled?: Not yet tested — will confirm.

- VS Code Version: 1.136.1
- OS Version: macOS 26.6.2 (build 25G83)
- Input Method: macOS built-in **Vietnamese - Telex** (`com.apple.inputmethod.VietnameseIM`, mode `com.apple.inputmethod.VietnameseTelex`)

## Summary

Typing letters/digits with the macOS built-in Vietnamese Telex input method inside the **integrated terminal** (and CLI programs spawned from it, e.g. Claude Code CLI) causes the current line/cursor to jump/shift down, as if a stray newline or reflow was inserted. Punctuation characters (which don't participate in Telex tone-mark composition) are unaffected.

This looks like the same class of bug as #239559 (Unikey/EVKey on Windows breaking IME in the editor), but reproduces in the **terminal panel** rather than the editor, on **macOS** rather than Windows, and with the **built-in system IME** rather than a third-party app.

## Scope already isolated

- ✅ Reproduces in VS Code integrated terminal running a plain zsh shell
- ✅ Reproduces when running the Claude Code CLI inside the integrated terminal
- ❌ Does NOT reproduce in any other VS Code editor tab (Monaco text editor)
- ❌ Does NOT reproduce in macOS `Terminal.app` or iTerm2 typing the same text with the same input method

This strongly suggests the terminal's own composition/marked-text handling (xterm.js) does not benefit from whatever fix/rework (`editor.experimentalEditContextEnabled` / EditContext API) resolved the analogous issue in the Monaco editor — the terminal appears to still use the older composition path.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. On macOS, enable "Vietnamese - Telex" as an input source (System Settings → Keyboard → Input Sources).
2. Open VS Code, open the integrated terminal (plain shell, e.g. zsh).
3. Switch to Vietnamese Telex and type a sentence containing plain letters/digits, e.g. `viet nam 123`.
4. Observe the current line/cursor being pushed down / a spurious line break appearing while typing letters or digits.
5. Type punctuation only (e.g. `,.;:`) — no issue occurs.
6. For comparison, do the same typing in a normal VS Code editor tab — no issue occurs.
7. For comparison, do the same typing in macOS `Terminal.app` — no issue occurs.

## Expected behavior

Typing with Telex in the integrated terminal should behave the same as in the editor tab or in `Terminal.app` — no spurious line jump.

## Actual behavior

The terminal line/cursor is pushed down while composing letters/digits via Telex.

## Config already ruled out

- `terminal.integrated.gpuAcceleration`: tried `on` and `off`, no difference
- `editor.accessibilitySupport`: tried `on`, no difference
- Confirmed via binary inspection there is no terminal-equivalent of `editor.experimentalEditContextEnabled`

## Possibly related

- #239559 (Unikey/EVKey breaking IME on Windows editor, fixed for editor via EditContext API but not applicable to terminal)
- #300251 / #301552 (IME composition overflow fixes in terminal, shipped in 1.112.0 — different symptom (overflow/clipping) but same subsystem, may be related root cause area)

title: Agent Host: provide inline editor context before send
body:
## Summary

- Actualize a bounded source window for editor inline chat inside the Agent Host immediately before provider dispatch.
- Keep the protocol selection attachment and browser/UI state unchanged.
- Mark `<editor_inline_context>` as current, authoritative source and tell the model to edit directly without a redundant read when it has sufficient context.
- Scope the behavior to the existing Agent Host chat-surface contribution.

The injected context is bounded to 16 lines, 220 characters per line, 4,096 rendered characters, and a 1 MiB source read. The target attachment is matched against the editor-inline surface URI so another selected attachment cannot be used accidentally.

## Performance investigation

We profiled repeated `comment out this line` requests in editor inline chat using Agent Host debug logs and CPU profiles.

| Stage | Original | Context only | Context + authoritative instruction | Final delta vs. original |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Session ready | 1.662s | 1.201s | 0.960s | -0.702s |
| Provider begins | 8.771s | 7.197s | 7.615s | -1.156s |
| First model call | 5.709s | 5.488s | 6.111s | +0.402s |
| `view` tool | 1.274s | 1.154s | eliminated | -1.274s |
| Tool-planning model call after `view` | 3.585s | 10.593s | eliminated | -3.585s |
| `edit` tool | 0.784s | 0.763s | 1.379s | +0.595s |
| Final model call | 3.056s | 2.936s | 2.707s | -0.349s |
| **Total** | **23.289s** | **28.241s** | **17.907s** | **-5.382s (-23.1%)** |

With context alone, the model still requested `view` for almost exactly the lines already present in `<editor_inline_context>`. After strengthening the instruction, the first model response was the `edit` call and the redundant `view` plus follow-up planning round trip disappeared.

The CPU captures were approximately 91-93% idle/program/GC, so the latency is dominated by SDK/runtime and model waits rather than Agent Host CPU work.

## MCP investigation and follow-up

The traces also showed roughly seven seconds before the first provider turn while 13 MCP servers started, authenticated, or failed/retried. This happened even though the session was definitively marked `vscode.chat.ephemeralSession: true`.

We tested all of the following for ephemeral sessions:

1. `enableConfigDiscovery: false`
2. omitting `mcpServers` instead of sending `{}`
3. additionally omitting `pluginDirectories`

None changed MCP startup: the same 13 servers still launched, including Azure, GitHub, Slack/WorkIQ, `vscode-tools`, `context7`, and the failing/retrying Docker-backed `awesome-copilot` server. The first request also remained around 45.8k uncached input tokens.

Those VS Code-side MCP experiments have been rolled back from this PR. We should instead add a Copilot SDK session option that acts as a master MCP switch: when disabled, the runtime must not discover, start, authenticate, or expose any MCP server regardless of config-directory discovery, plugin directories, explicit server maps, or runtime defaults. VS Code can then set that option for ephemeral inline-chat sessions.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client`
- Focused Agent Host suites previously passed 388 tests during implementation.
- After the final instruction update, 372 tests passed and one stale expected-instruction assertion failed; that assertion was updated before commit and was not rerun at the requester's direction.
- Pre-commit hygiene passed for all changed files.

title: agentHost: Resolve published MCP server lifecycle IDs
body:
Fixes #332072

## Problem

Agent Host start/stop handling reverse-resolved customization IDs only through the controller's runtime `_live` inventory. During a same-name collision, the runtime can first associate a server name with a published plugin child and then receive a distinct same-name workspace top-level customization.

Agent Customizations presents the workspace entry and sends its exact ID, but the live lookup no longer recognizes that ID. The provider logs `Cannot start unknown MCP server customization ...`, no server process starts, and the optimistic client reducer leaves the row at `Starting`.

## Change

Keep the runtime lookup as the first choice, then fall back to an exact-ID lookup across the session's currently published customizations.

The fallback accepts only an ID that is present in current session state. It does not add a broad same-name alias and does not change collision precedence. The SDK lifecycle API remains name-keyed, so it starts the effective server winner already selected for that name.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `npx mocha test/unit/node/index.js --delay --ui=tdd --timeout=20000 --exit --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/shared/mcpCustomizationController.test.ts` — 20 passing
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check`
- Regression coverage verifies published IDs resolve before the SDK has populated the live inventory and unknown IDs remain rejected.
- Deterministic live Code OSS A/B with a real Copilot Agent Host session and real local stdio MCP processes:
  - A host-only plugin published and started `dupe`; the real UI then stopped it through its plugin-child customization ID.
  - A workspace-root `.mcp.json` with another `dupe` was published afterward, producing two distinct current customization IDs with no synthetic `mcp-top-level:*` ID and no intervening SDK state event that could repair the mapping.
  - Unpatched main: the UI dispatched `SessionMcpServerStartRequested` with the exact workspace ID, Agent Host logged the matching unknown-customization warning, no process spawned, and the clicked row remained stuck at `Starting`.
  - Patched: the UI dispatched the same workspace ID, no unknown-customization warning was logged, a new real MCP process spawned, the workspace entry transitioned `stopped -> starting -> ready`, and the clicked row reached `Running`.
  - A separate `solo` server completed stop/start successfully as a control.
- The patched live arm was repeated through the repository's normal `scripts/code.bat` launch path with the same result.

Current source combines user and `.vscode/mcp.json` inputs before Agent Host receives them, so the live harness used a host-configured plugin child plus workspace-root `.mcp.json` to deterministically reproduce the same published child/top-level identity collision described by the issue.

title: mcp: Activate lazy providers in Agent Customizations
body:
Fixes #327317

## Problem

Extension-contributed MCP providers are registered as uncached lazy collections with no initial server definitions. Opening **Agent Customizations > MCP Servers** refreshed the already-materialized server list but did not activate those collections, so the provider extension remained inactive and its servers were absent.

Running another discovery command such as **MCP: List Servers** activated the same provider and made the server appear, which explains why reinstalling or interacting with the regular VS Code MCP surface temporarily repaired the Agent Customizations list.

## Change

Activate MCP collections when the MCP management section becomes visible and when MCP access is restored while that section is already visible.

Activation remains scoped to explicit user intent: this does not eagerly activate MCP providers during workbench startup. It is gated by MCP access, repeated visibility notifications remain idempotent, and provider activation failures are surfaced through the notification service.

## Validation

- `npm run gulp compile-client`
- `scripts/test.bat --run src\vs\workbench\contrib\chat\test\browser\aiCustomization\mcpListWidget.test.js` — 43 passing
- Targeted ESLint and `git diff --check`
- Added coverage for:
  - activation on the first visible transition;
  - no activation while MCP access is disabled;
  - activation when access is restored while visible;
  - user-visible activation errors.
- Live Code OSS A/B with an isolated profile and a lazy extension-contributed MCP provider:
  - Unpatched: opening Agent Customizations left the provider inactive and the server absent; running **MCP: List Servers** activated it and made the server appear.
  - Patched: opening the MCP section activated the provider immediately and showed the server before any discovery command was run.

title: Update MCP commands to use new configuration locations
body:
This pull request updates the MCP commands to work with new configuration file locations, replacing the old `.vscode/mcp.json` and user data `mcp.json` paths. The changes include:

- **Schema Support**:
  - Introduced support for the `mcpServers` schema while ensuring legacy configurations remain readable.

- **Validation**:
  - All relevant tests have been updated and successfully passed, ensuring that the new configurations work as intended without introducing regressions.

This implementation enhances the MCP command functionality by aligning it with the new configuration structure, improving user experience and maintainability.
